content_units: Uneven Cooling in a 95 m² Flat

You likely have an   airflow or balancing issue first  , and the overdue   filter change   is the strongest easy-to-fix suspect. In a third-floor apartment, solar heat gain and a longer duct run to one bedroom can also make one room stay warm while the living room overcools.
Most Likely Causes and Safe Checks
Issue   Why it fits your symptoms   Safe DIY check   What would point to service

Dirty return filter   11 months without change can reduce airflow and worsen room-to-room imbalance   Remove and inspect filter; if gray/dust-packed, replace with same size/spec   Weak airflow improves only slightly after filter replacement

Closed/partly closed supply or return vents   Warm bedroom may not be getting enough air; living room may be taking too much   Confirm all vents are fully open and not blocked by curtains/furniture   One room still has clearly weaker airflow with vents fully open

Duct imbalance or disconnected/leaky branch duct   Common when one room is persistently warm while another is very cold   Hold a tissue near each supply vent to compare airflow strength room to room   Bedroom airflow is much weaker than nearby rooms

Thermostat placement bias   If thermostat is in the cold living room, system may shut off before bedroom cools   Note whether thermostat is near a supply vent, sunny wall, TV, or kitchen heat   Temperature near thermostat is much cooler than bedroom at same time

High heat gain in the bedroom   Third-floor rooms can run hotter from sun/roof/wall exposure   Check window sun exposure, blinds, curtains, and door position during hottest hours   Bedroom heats fast again even when AC is running normally

Evaporator/condenser performance issue   Low airflow, coil dirt, or refrigerant issues can reduce cooling to farther rooms first   Look/listen only: ice on lines, unusual hissing, outdoor unit struggling, weak overall cooling   Ice, poor cooling across multiple rooms, short cycling, or long nonstop runtime
Home Checks You Can Do Today
Option 1: Replace the air filter   Most cost-effective first step; overdue by normal maintenance standards   Likely under $15–$35
Find filter size
Option 2: Airflow comparison room by room   Use a tissue or your hand at each vent; note strongest and weakest vents   Confirms imbalance fast
Vent checklist
Option 3: Thermostat and room temperature check   Compare thermostat reading with bedroom and living room temps after 20–30 minutes of runtime   Helps identify sensor/location bias
Thermostat tips
Option 4: Heat-gain check in the warm bedroom   Close blinds/curtains, keep door open, check if afternoon sun is the trigger   Distinguishes AC issue vs room load issue
Cooling tips
What to Tell the HVAC Technician
Give a short, specific report so the visit stays within your    $180 diagnostic budget  :
- Apartment:   95-square-meter third-floor flat
- System:   central air, one outdoor unit
- Main symptom:   one bedroom stays warm while living room gets very cold
- Maintenance note:   air filter has not been changed in 11 months
- Pattern: mention   time of day  ,   sun-facing bedroom  , and whether the problem is   constant or worse in afternoons
- Airflow note: say whether the bedroom vent feels   weaker   than living room vents
- Thermostat note: include   where thermostat is located
- Unit behavior: mention   long runtimes, short cycling, strange noise, ice, water leaks, or weak cooling throughout home
- Access note: tell them whether this is an   apartment/managed property   and if outdoor unit/air handler access is restricted
Ask the tech to prioritize:
-   Diagnostic only first, capped near $180
-   Filter/airflow/static pressure check
-   Supply temperature split
-   Duct airflow/balancing to the warm bedroom
-   Coil and refrigerant performance check if airflow looks normal
Best Use of Your $180 Diagnostic Budget
With your symptoms, the best sequence is:
-   First:   replace filter and fully open/unblock all vents
-   Second:   document room temperatures and airflow differences
-   Third:   book a diagnostic visit only if the bedroom still runs warm

A sensible service goal is:   confirm whether this is a basic airflow/balancing issue or a mechanical cooling issue  . If the filter is the main problem, you may solve most of it without spending the diagnostic fee.
